title: How the Annual Flood Premium on a Summit Reserve Is Projected at Review
content:
Set-Aside Accounts, Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve: the projected annual flood premium held on file after a review of the reserve's flood insurance bills is defined as follows.

| Quantity | Definition |
|---|---|
| Flood bills of the review | The flood insurance bills on file for the reserve received no later than the review date and fewer than 12 whole calendar months before it |
| Current flood premium | The billed amount of the paid flood insurance bill with the latest due date |
| Flood renewal loading | The renewal increase of 4.0 percent plus the flood premium-change loading, the flood residence loading and the flood appraisal loading, all in percent and added together; those three loadings are each zero |
| Renewal flood premium | The current flood premium increased once by the flood renewal loading, applied once to the current flood premium and not one loading after another |
| Flood renewal share | One half (0.5) |
| Projected annual flood premium | The current flood premium times one less the flood renewal share, plus the renewal flood premium times the flood renewal share, rounded half up to the cent once, at the end |

The review relies on the flood insurance bill on file with the latest due date.

**Worked figures on a hypothetical latest-due paid flood bill of 950.00.** Renewal flood premium: 950.00 increased by 4.0 percent, 988.00. Projected annual flood premium: 950.00 times one half plus 988.00 times one half, 475.00 plus 494.00, which is 969.00.
